body.statement: For \(\mathcal W^{(2)}\), the untreated mean has rank one, \(\mu_{2,0}=\mu_{2,1}=1\), \(A_{2,0}=A_{2,1}=4\), and \(B_2=1\). At each horizon, the four treated target cells have coefficient \(1/4\), the four donor target cells have coefficient \(-1/4\), and the four treated pre-period cells shared by both horizons have coefficient \(-1/4\). Therefore each marginal variance is \(12(1/4)^2=3/4\), each shared-cell covariance product is \((-1/4)(-1/4)=1/16\), the off-diagonal covariance is \(4/16=1/4\), and the correlation is \((1/4)/(3/4)=1/3\). This explicitly satisfies the noncancellation condition in \(\mathrm{lem:staircase\mbox{-}covariance}\).
body.justification: The fully enumerated finite panel verifies the coefficient normalization and exhibits a nonzero signed shared-cell sum without appealing to an unnamed procedure.
body.gap: No located low-rank staggered-adoption inference result displays this exact two-horizon coefficient calculation; the proposition is an algebraic witness, not a claim that a published method imposes block independence.
body.consumer: The twelve-cell calculation is a deterministic unit test for implementations of the full RTC-law event covariance.
